summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of osteoporosis, coronary artery disease, and chronic back pain was admitted with acute back pain found to be due to a new T12 vertebral compression fracture. She was managed non-operatively with a TLSO brace, pain control, and physical therapy. Her hospital course was complicated by C. difficile colitis, likely triggered by recent antibiotic use, which was treated with oral vancomycin. She also had transient hypoxia due to atelectasis, mild acute kidney injury from dehydration, and chronic thrombocytopenia. Urinary frequency was evaluated and found not to be infectious. She improved clinically, was stabilized on her chronic medications, and was discharged to inpatient rehabilitation to continue recovery and complete her antibiotic course.
problems: Other osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter for fracture
Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, not specified as recurrent
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
